parallel.requirements: Recognized the task as a full installable Jinja2 project with complete source tree, pyproject metadata, API exports, docs, examples, tests, and submit/verification expectations.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent kept implementation, assembly, integration, and verification ownership while delegating release/version and submit-harness reconnaissance to child agents.
parallel.implementation: Parent cloned upstream Jinja, compared main and 3.1.6, chose the stable 3.1.6 baseline, copied the repository tree, patched pyproject.toml and src/jinja2/__init__.py, and added support files from main where useful.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Parent removed temporary clones, delivered a single workspace tree, and final response described the complete package with top-level exports and project metadata aligned to the prompt.
parallel.verification: Parent ran editable install, the full bundled pytest suite with 909 passing tests, and an import/export sanity check for Environment, Template, SandboxedEnvironment, NativeEnvironment, Extension, nodes, and contextfilter.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official unfinished behavior remains: the run did not find a local submit command, but the current official evaluation later completed and passed 911/911.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same full Jinja2 package, metadata, API, examples, tests, and submit expectations without delegation.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single agent owned all stages: downloading the 3.1.6 sdist, inspecting metadata and APIs, copying sources, editing support files, testing, fixing examples, and final delivery.
serial.implementation: Downloaded the 3.1.6 source distribution, copied it into /workspace, adjusted pyproject metadata, added support files and examples, fixed the debugger example, and removed stale PKG-INFO.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Integrated everything directly in the final workspace and final response summarized the complete source tree, metadata, examples, and installability.
serial.verification: Ran a representative subset, then full PYTHONPATH pytest with 909 passing tests, reran after metadata edits, checked examples, performed editable install, and checked submit availability.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official unfinished behavior remains: submit was unavailable during the agent session, but the current official evaluation completed and passed 911/911.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the full project, dependency, API export, examples/tests, and submit requirements and delivered a Jinja2 package.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements from the byte-identical prompt and delivered the same broad project surface.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference; both satisfied the official evaluator, with minor internal differences in support files and source acquisition path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used child agents for release and submit reconnaissance while the parent retained implementation, integration, and verification ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents and kept the entire download, edit, verify, and delivery pipeline in one thread.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had reconnaissance delegation but not delegated implementation; serial was a single-owner control. The ownership difference did not change the official outcome.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child handoffs concerned version and submit availability; no child produced a code component requiring an interface contract with parent work.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no cross-agent context boundary and made its own 3.1.6, metadata, and verification decisions locally.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a child recommendation that favored main for prompt shape while acknowledging 3.1.6 as latest release, but the parent's stable 3.1.6 decision was independently verified and passed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel began from a git clone, then downloaded and cloned the 3.1.6 tag, copied the stable tree, and patched pyproject.toml and __init__.py.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial downloaded the 3.1.6 sdist, copied it directly, then patched pyproject.toml, added support files/examples/assets, fixed the debugger example, and removed PKG-INFO.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both converged on upstream 3.1.6; serial did more explicit support-file/example construction, while parallel mixed stable tag code with a few dev-branch support files and API export patches.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The release-check child and submit-probe grandchild both reached final answers, and the parent continued to final delivery after receiving the release-check result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; all findings and fixes stayed inside one continuous thread.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had additional result receipt steps, but no completed implementation result was lost, unjoined, or merged after verification.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent was the only actor observed making final source/config edits, copied final support assets, cleaned temporary clones, and assembled one workspace tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial edited one workspace directly, with three patch phases and no concurrent writers.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had shared workspace visibility for child reconnaissance but no observed write collision, overwrite, or artifact contamination; serial avoided that risk by construction.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran editable install, the full bundled suite with 909 passing tests, an API export sanity check, and later passed the official 911-test evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran subsets, full pytest, fixed a failing example, reran tests/examples, installed editable, and later passed the official 911-test evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had sufficient acceptance evidence; serial's local verification was broader around examples, while parallel added explicit top-level export sanity checks.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel finished in about 313 agent seconds, used child reconnaissance, briefly waited once, then closed after local tests and submit-command lookup.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished in about 262 agent seconds with no subagents, no timeout, and closed after tests, examples, install, and submit-command lookup.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used more tokens/time and child activity, but not enough to cause budget exhaustion or omit required finalization; both closed with passing official evaluations.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome. The current completed status.json evaluation for both modes reports solution_passed true with 911 passed out of 911 total tests. The parallel run's extra coordination consisted of release and submit reconnaissance, while the parent still built, integrated, verified, and delivered the implementation. The serial run achieved the same outcome through a single-agent sdist-based path.
parallel_contributors: Parent-owned implementation from upstream Jinja2 3.1.6 with metadata and API export patches.
Child reconnaissance informed version and submit-harness context without becoming an implementation dependency.
Local editable install, 909-test run, and export sanity check before closure.
serial_contributors: Single-agent download and copy of the 3.1.6 sdist into /workspace.
Metadata/support-file/example edits, including a debugger example fix before closure.
Subset, full-suite, example, and editable-install verification before final response.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel mixed git-clone inspection with a stable tag copy and copied a few support assets from main; serial used the 3.1.6 sdist directly and manually added support files.
Serial caught and fixed an example-script bug that parallel did not separately exercise, but both final artifacts passed official tests.

Reject: the relevant parent file changes were in place before install, pytest, and export checks; no child implementation was merged after verification.
Reject: no child produced a delegated implementation to retrieve or merge; child outputs were reconnaissance findings, and parent implementation was already integrated.
Reject: the submit-probe verifier result returned to the release-check child and the release-check final returned to the parent; no concrete verifier finding was trapped below the parent.
Reject: no required child failed, aborted, or was cancelled; the only transient wait timeout was followed by normal continuation and eventual child completion.
Reject: the child result was visible and arguably not adopted in full, but it was not needed for a passing solution and caused no adverse inconsistency or omitted work.
Reject: the parent briefly attempted a 10 second wait, then inspected and continued work; it did not wait blindly until deadline while actionable progress sat uninspected.
Reject: no concurrent agents produced competing implementations or overlapping build ownership across different files; children performed read-only reconnaissance.
Reject: no two live agents edited the same source or configuration file and no reconciliation of concurrent same-file changes appears.
